title: Milvus + WP — E2E Search / Query
description: Proxy → Delegator / TSafe → scheduling → segment execution → result return. Ordered operational steps; see E2E-DASHBOARDS.md for metric scope and coverage.

panels.title: E2E Search / Query — read from top to bottom

options.content:
**Proxy → Delegator / TSafe → scheduling → segment execution → result return**

Select a time window containing the workload. Channel filters apply to Milvus channel metrics; log filters apply to WP metrics. They are independent identities: use wpcli metadata to map them; there is no automatic channel-to-log or collection-to-log join. Legends identify the actual process.

**No data ≠ healthy zero.** Lazy/error/remote-only metrics may be absent; `./stack.sh verify` records each stage's coverage. Timers overlap and quantiles are not additive. Read each step's guidance before interpreting an idle signal.

Start from request status, observation count and successful latency. Strong consistency can wait for ingestion visibility; use stage 2 and the WAL Read/Consume dashboard when TSafe dominates. These server timers do not include the SDK/network round trip.

panels.title: Successful Proxy search/query latency
panels.description: P50/P95/P99 of observed operations; no observations produce no data/NaN. Check the stage's observation rate. Quantiles from different stages cannot be added or subtracted. Values above the largest finite histogram bucket cannot be resolved accurately.

panels.title: 2. Delegator — wait for visibility and route work

options.content: TSafe wait means the required consistency timestamp is not yet serviceable; compare consumption lag instead of immediately blaming vector execution. Querynode-prefixed metrics can originate on SN. The actual Pod/component remains in each legend.

panels.title: 3. Execution scheduling — queue versus available concurrency

options.content: Rising queue delay with a growing ready queue suggests scheduling/resource pressure. Compare execution time in stage 4. Scheduler families depend on the Milvus image and which node executes the work; missing series are reported as coverage gaps.

panels.title: 4. Segment execution — core work and loading

options.content: Compare core/segment execution and segment loading. Growing and sealed work can run in different processes; preserve component and segment-state labels. Loading a segment is a different timer population from an individual search, so do not add their quantiles.

panels.title: 5. Result return — downstream reduction and Proxy merge/decode

options.content: If execution is stable but result waiting grows, inspect fan-out, routing and the slowest responding node. Proxy wait includes downstream work and transport; it is not a pure network latency. Large reductions/decode can reflect result size or fan-out.
